text:
Before you start:

Choose a poem to learn.

You might have your own book of poetry, or you could visit the library and find out what poetry books they have. You could also find a poem online - one of our favourite poems to learn is 'Now We Are Six' by A.A. Milne!

Tip: A shorter poem can be easier for your first try!

The activity:

  1. Read through the poem together and talk about what it means.
    If you really understand what the poem is about, it makes it easier to remember the words.
  2. Look for any patterns in the poem that might make it easier to remember.
    Does it have any repeated words? Does it rhyme?
  3. Read the first line and then say it again without looking.
    Sometimes adding actions can really help you remember the words.
  4. Once you can remember the first line, try the first two lines together.
    Building up sections of the poem together helps remember them in the right order.
  5. Once you can remember the whole poem, practise it several times.
    It should get stuck in your head!
  6. When you know it really well, try performing your poem!
    You could perform it to someone in your family, a friend or even make a video!
